title: [performance] A base warm that an integrator restart cuts off is warmed again, for its source's main as it is then, by the integrator that starts next
prompt:
Read crates/spawn-cli/src/integrate/warm.rs (the module's docs, `Warms::start` with its pid file, `take_over`, `Left`, `want`, `poll`), integrate.rs (`with_warm`, `want_warm`, `poll_warm`, `warm_dir`) and scripts/rsi/gate.sh's base cache ("The base cache", "When a warm and a gate share a base", the test listing entry).

The problem (rev-f, 2026-11-12 16:25; sync/backlog.md S30). The integrator's landing-time base warm (`gate.sh --base-only` after a landing or an owner's move) runs as its child under `setpriv --pdeathsig TERM`. So every restart of spawn-integrate kills the warm in flight, and a deploy restarts it with almost every landing group. The next integrator reads the warm's pid file, says "the base warm of <commit> (pid …) a previous integrator started is gone (no such process); nothing stopped", and drops the commit. Nothing warms that main again: a warm is only wanted for a landing seen during the integrator's own life. On 11-12 the 66dc88cf warm started at 16:03:44 and died at the 16:05:36 deploy. The next gate on 66dc88cf (16:21) said "the base's listing is not in the cache (none): listed now", spent 77 s on the listing and judged the base cold. A warm that finishes (979d4173) leaves the 1491-test listing and 56 base results in the cache. The same happened at 15:21 for 47348208. This is separate from the deploy's own warm of the deployed head (deploy.sh, fixed by 628ea5ef).

Required behaviour.
(a) A warm's pid file also records its source and its scenarios directory, beside its pid, start time and commit.
(b) A starting integrator that finds a pid file warms again, at its first passes, the base of that warm's source's main as it is now, with that warm's scenarios. This applies whether the warm is gone or the take-over stopped it.
- When main has not moved, that is the lost warm's commit.
- When main has moved, it is main's new commit. A main the lost warm had is never warmed in place of the current one.
- It is wanted like any warm (`want`): one at a time, started when the source's mirror has the commit, abandoned when main moves on, under the parent-death signal, and not started during a drain.
- The integrator says which commit it warms again and why ("the base warm of <commit> … was cut off: warming <source>'s main <commit>").
(c) A pid file that names no source (an older integrator's) warms nothing again, and the integrator says so. A pid file that is not a warm's is as today.
(d) The warm still never outlives the integrator unaccounted for (the module's three guarantees stay). This objective adds no unit and no detached process: the next integrator finishes the work.
No gate verdict, landing or record depends on a warm.

Acceptance: rsi/scenarios/096.sh. The world: a gated mission on one source, judged by a recording gate (SPAWN_GATE). A candidate is accepted. A base warm notes its start and pid, holds until its release file, then writes a test listing entry and a scenario result into the base cache ($XDG_CACHE_HOME/spawn/gate-base) as gate.sh does, and notes its end. Integrators are stopped with TERM, as a restart stops them. Checks:
- (1) the task is gated and lands (main L), and the integrator starts the warm of L;
- (2) TERM: the integrator and its warm are gone within 10 s, and the warm never ended;
- (3) a second integrator on the same root starts a warm of L within 30 s;
- (4) while that warm holds, the source's main moves to M (an owner's commit) and the second integrator gets TERM. A third integrator starts a warm of M within 30 s, and none of L. Released, it ends, and M's listing and result entries are in the base cache.
It fails with 1 on 47348208 (live): (1) and (2) pass, then the next integrator says the warm "is gone …; nothing stopped" and starts none, at (3) and at (4). Its throwaway is sync/obj-096/throwaway.diff. A mutant that re-warms the recorded commit in place of main's current one fails (4).

The product reason. Each restart that cuts a warm off costs the next gate on that main its whole base phase, including the 77 s test listing, and restarts come with almost every landing group. Gates are the bottleneck of the fleet's throughput: the performance line's gate time and report to live both carry this.

Rules: never edit the protected paths, which the gate rejects: rsi/, scripts/ (scripts/rsi/, scripts/blackbox/, scripts/e2e.sh among them), deploy/, all of web/ except web/src/, web/test/ and web/index.html, rust-toolchain files and .cargo/. The gate also rejects fewer runnable tests than the base, any lint relaxation and any build-time code. The gate builds offline from the cargo caches already on the host. Keep every existing check green (037, 008, 035 and check-j11-push-drain run the integrator) and add tests of your own for the new behaviour:
- a warm.rs unit test of the pid file's new fields, and of take-over's answer for each case: gone with a source, still running with a source, no source, not a warm's file, and main moved;
- an integrate test that the warm wanted at start is started at the first pass, and not during a drain.
